scope: 960 native RGB outputs per policy, eight previously examined regression sources, unchanged big2k weights and tuning; not blind release validation or browser cadence

default_regression.interpretation: Exact native RGB byte regression; includes same model, stage tuning, sender and PNG decode.

parity.scope: FP32 native Metal probes against Torch policy emulation; no native quality or timing claim
parity.interpretation: Strict parity receipts retain failures in newly added brightness-ramp TAA fixtures. The old and new default shader have identical rows, including the 1.5229e-5 error. All motion fields and all original fixtures pass. No tolerance or fixture changed. Native RGB regression and quality comparison remain required.

limitations: Negative LPIPS/DISTS changes are better; fine correlation is higher-better. Metrics supplement image review.

Timing includes native preprocessing, model and detail only, excludes input decode, sender packing, disk, transport and browser presentation. Capture order is not randomized; separate matched timing repeats are required to quantify small runtime changes.
No weights or shipping defaults changed. Strict FP32 parity failures on new TAA ramps are retained; all motion fields pass and default native RGB exactly matches the frozen baseline.

final_math_validation.basis: Unchanged shader reaches1.523e-5 on the new low-variance ramp; TAA variance is sensitive to FP32 reduction roundoff. Limit2e-5 is0.0051 of one RGB8 code value. Initial strict1e-5 failures retained, all960 native default RGBs match their frozen baseline. No fixtures or motion-field tolerance changed.

visual_review.selection: Six preselected frame100 h264350kbps crops; additionally inspected largest gain-only LPIPS gain/regression and the OldTown exception, explicitly selected after scoring.
visual_review.observations: Small changes in local boundaries and texture; no dramatic recovery of the fine reference detail. Full search has the strongest broad native spatial metrics. These results support an incremental motion-policy improvement, not a breakthrough claim.
